transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello there, Doctor. Nice to meet you. You know, I was just looking at the magazines out in the waiting room. They had an old issue of Popular Mechanics from a few years back, and it got me thinking about my old Ford truck. Used to spend hours under the hood of that thing. My grandson, he's always telling me I should get a new one, but they just don't make 'em like they used to, you know? All computers now. 

But, uh, what was I saying? Right, why I'm here. Well, it's just... what brings me in is that whenever I step into a slow elevator or one of those small locked rooms, my chest jumps right away. I get this strong need to get back out before I can even think straight. It's like my heart just takes off. Speaking of taking off, my daughter took a flight to Florida last week. Said the weather was just beautiful. I haven't been to Florida since... oh, it must have been '98. Or maybe '99? We drove down, took the scenic route. Took us three days...
Do you ever feel that same chest tightness or racing heart in other situations, like in crowded places, open spaces, or when you're not in an elevator or small room?

Crowds? No, no, crowds don't bother me none. I used to go to the state fair every summer, shoulder to shoulder with folks. Best funnel cake you ever had, right over by the Ferris wheel. My wife, she loved the Ferris wheel. We'd go up and you could see the whole county from up there, all the way to the highway. 

But no, out in the open or in a big crowd, my chest is just fine. It's really just... well, those little spaces. I mean, I know a little storage room or that elevator at the museum isn't the same as being locked up in a prison or something. I know that in my head. But my mind, it just treats it like trouble the minute I see there's no window and that door shuts tight. 

Speaking of the museum, my granddaughter took me there a couple weeks ago to see the old airplanes. They had a real P-51 Mustang hanging right there from the ceiling. Beautiful machine. The way they built those engines back then, it was real craftsmanship, you know? Not like the plastic they use today. We stood there looking at it for a good twenty minutes...

latest_inference.note: The patient specifically experiences anxiety in enclosed spaces (elevators, small locked rooms), without panic attacks or generalized anxiety. This points toward a specific phobia, particularly situational or claustrophobia, ruling out other anxiety and depressive disorders.
